audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[0..6].side read "Skill" on every row while content win[] and the packet levelChart read Ahri, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Skill, Ahri.
audit.why: Level 1 is genuinely yours — Qiyana has no ranged tool at all and must walk into a 970-range orb — and the late game is yours once terrain stops deciding fights. Showing "Skill" on those two rows in one layer and "Ahri" in the other is two answers to the same question.
audit.corrected: phases[0].side and phases[6].side flipped to Ahri to match win[0] and win[6]; the five middle rows were already in agreement and were left alone.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] and whys[5] built her first-item spike on "Recurve Bow/Serrated Dirk".
audit.why: Recurve Bow is an attack-speed component and has no place on an AD assassin's build — a reader watching her item bar for it will never see it, and will therefore never see the spike coming. Serrated Dirk is the real early buy.
audit.corrected: Rewritten around Serrated Dirk and the lethality line it builds into.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three ability errors in the interaction text. Her element pickup was called "E-Q"; her ultimate was said to "root" and to "reset her E dash on takedown"; and breakdown.cooldowns claimed that once Audacity is spent "she cannot reach you". The packet also flags that none of her six ability names appear anywhere.
audit.why: Terrashape (W) is the 1100-range dash that enchants her weapon off terrain — that is the ability tied to walls and brush, not E. Audacity (E) is a 650-range dash to an enemy, 11 seconds at rank 1. Supreme Display of Talent (R) is a 950-range shockwave that knocks up and stuns; Riot's text says nothing about a root or a dash reset, so neither can be asserted. And because Terrashape is itself a 1100-range dash on 7 seconds, "once Audacity is spent she cannot reach you" is simply false — she has a longer dash than the one you were told to count.
audit.corrected: Terrashape named as the element/terrain ability, the ultimate described as a knockup-and-stun, and the cooldown section rebuilt around both of her dashes.
sources: enemyKit Q/W/E/R text, range and cd

audit.whatIsWrong: Qiyana was written as "his"/"he" throughout the full layer; "Fox Fire" appeared for Fox-Fire; dosFull[2].d cited a "fifteen-second" Audacity cooldown.
audit.why: Audacity is 11/10/9/8/7 — a player stepping up on a fifteen-second count steps into a dash that came back four seconds ago.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed, Fox-Fire hyphenated, cooldown corrected to eleven seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you and wants.foe each had only three entries where the structure carries four.

audit.corrected: Filled both with "before": null, grounded in Royal Privilege's first-hit bonus and Terrashape's terrain requirement.

notes: The packet's defect line was right: not one of Qiyana's six ability names appeared in the matchup. Three real errors beyond that. (1) Her terrain/element ability was consistently called 'E' — it is Terrashape (W), a 1100-range dash, while Audacity (E) is the 650-range gap-close; that mislabel propagates into every piece of positioning advice on the page. (2) breakdown.cooldowns told the reader that once Audacity is spent 'she cannot reach you', which is false — Terrashape is a longer dash on a shorter cooldown. (3) 'Recurve Bow' was named as her first-item spike; it is an attack-speed component with no place in a lethality build. Also removed: the claim that her ultimate roots and resets her E on takedown — Riot's text says knock up and stun, and says nothing about a reset, so it is not asserted here either way. wants.you and wants.foe each had a missing fourth entry; both filled from Royal Privilege's first-hit bonus. Left unasserted: whether Charm is cleansable or tenacity-reduced, and whether Audacity's cooldown genuinely resets on takedown (widely believed, not in the kit text).
